title: The War for Pristinia
dek: The bridge, the failed raid, Melian’s disappearance and Elenia’s earthquake: a town survives bombardment while its defenders divide over loyalty, mercy and the cost of another retreat.

facts.Recorded dates: 7 and 25–29, Month of Physisia, Year 2; investigation on 4, Month of Rebirth; remaining-engine assault on 11, Month of Rebirth. The earlier siege-breaking intervention retains its unresolved exact date.
facts.Setting: Pristinia; Prima · Pristinia walls; Prima · Melian’s House; Pristinia; Prima

body:
Before the Rahu engines can break Pristinia’s walls, the war has already divided its adventurers. A companion becomes an informer, a bridge defense disintegrates, and a raid reaches the machines only to leave its attackers dead or retreating. The town survives, but the story of its survival includes the people who do not come home from each fight.

The price of being useful

On 7, Month of Physisia, Year 2, Magnus Niriin tries to accompany Ambassador Sophina to a meeting with Captain Jeele. He offers assistance, presents himself as a Rahu ally and hopes to watch the bargaining. Sophina lets him travel to the docks, but permission to follow is narrower than he wants. The negotiations are private. When he keeps pressing for access, she rebukes him and he steps back.

His opening comes through information instead. He later tells Sophina that someone intends to thwart the agreement by freeing Ahau slaves being traded with the pirates. This is his report of a plan; the exchange does not show a completed rescue. It does show the effect of his warning. Sophina signals her guards, Jeele cries out about a spy, and the captain prepares to sail. Sophina thanks Magnus and tells him his good deed will be remembered.

A recent adventuring companion has made himself useful to the force that will attack Pristinia. He has not been admitted to every confidence, but he has already chosen whose business to protect. By the time that choice becomes open violence, the town’s defenders will be facing someone who knows them.

The bridge before the engines

On 25, Month of Physisia, scouts bring word that the main Rahu advance is coming toward the bridge, with engines behind it and skirmishes elsewhere. Lilian has lost the road toward The Before and is preparing evacuation. Ruben and the Ale-Chemy Knights will defend the town and help those unable to escape under their own power.

The adventurers disagree about where to meet the attack. Carmen wants the engines; Ghilsen suggests destroying the bridge. Fulmin weighs the defenses while Fredrick offers Carmen support. Lilian does not give the adventurers a single binding order. They must choose how to use the help they can actually bring.

Magnus is already on the other side. He privately warns Brianna that the bridge is trapped and asks her not to name him. She passes on the warning. The warning is witnessed; the trap itself is not confirmed by this exchange. Meanwhile the company approaches through portable defenses, and the catapults keep coming.

A companion under the bridge

An unnatural storm rises over the field. Fredrick finds Magnus concealed beneath the bridge and tells Carmen. She asks Paco to watch him while she keeps her attention on the enemy ahead. Magnus makes that division impossible: he flies at Carmen and attacks. He calls his choice the right thing to do. Carmen answers with magic, briefly banishing him through a hellish portal before turning back toward the advance.

The bombardment does not stop for their quarrel. Stones strike adventurers as well as defenses. When Carmen sees Brianna healing Magnus, she calls Paco and Ramon away. Brianna wants him alive for trial; Carmen sees an active enemy being returned to the fight. Fredrick’s appeal cannot reconcile them. Carmen makes another attack and withdraws, later laying down obscuring fog even as the stones continue to hit her and her companions.

Fredrick stabs the unconscious Magnus. The narration gives Magnus a last breath. Carmen herself falls and gasps for help; this scene does not establish her death. Then Magnus stands again, laughing and taunting. The narration subsequently places him where Fredrick had been, without explaining the return’s mechanism. Another collapse of the Rahu line does not undo the company’s losses. Brianna cannot rise after another impact; Ruben shoots Magnus down again as the survivors try to get away.

The engines survive this defense. So does the argument over what mercy requires when an enemy has been a friend. Neither a healing spell nor an execution attempt produces the clean ending its caster or wielder wanted.

Decisions while the stones fall

By 29, Month of Physisia, the war is inside Pristinia’s homes. The Rahu are firing corpses as well as ordinary ammunition. Townspeople and Knights fight fires, wounded people need shelter, and a boulder crashes into a nearby house while the adventurers are still deciding how to act. The house proves empty. Elsewhere, Scarlett is carrying water until she is close to collapse.

A refuge below ground offers room for injured people, valuables and frightened families, if it can be made ready. Water, bedding, digging and support beams matter as urgently as weapons. Nimueh helps Scarlett; Jon works on supports; Stella and Sola attend to children. Ghilsen tries to organize the work, but the townspeople have already begun it. Their labor is not waiting for an adventurer to invent rescue.

Oya asks Aravil to move the preparation for an attack away from the shelter. Gathering armed people beside those hiding from bombardment could draw the danger straight to them. Aravil fears that every delay costs the town another house. Sajhan has carried enough bodies and wants a way to strike back. The dispute takes place above people who need the ceiling to hold.

Melian’s earlier defense account places her at the Northeast Tower, organizing around the town’s terrain, palisades and workers. Ada remembers her as Pristinia’s last banner. Around that public image are the less celebrated tasks now keeping its residents alive: finding water, putting out a roof and holding up a tunnel.

Brianna carries them over the walls

Brianna offers a way out that does not require opening the defenses. She can turn the party into mist. It is a means of travel rather than an immediate fighting form: they will need time to become solid again. Sajhan asks whether each traveler will be able to move independently. Aravil intends to go over the wall toward the northwest, where the barrage is coming from.

When Brianna casts, the company rises out of the town in clouds. Sajhan uses smoke from the burning buildings as cover and gains height. Beyond the walls she finds a clearing with siege engines near a creek. The Rahu do not detect the mist. She sends the position to her companions, and the scattered travelers converge.

Close reconnaissance changes the problem. The engines are reinforced wood, and the tar Nimueh hopes to exploit is inside covered ballista towers. Some soldiers look strangely tired; the party does not learn why. Sajhan worries about a trap. Others want to preserve enough magic for a retreat. They have reached the machines, but reaching them has not made destroying them easy.

The tower burns; the raid fails

The alarm goes up as the adventurers become solid. Oya throws up a magical screen for Pappy and calls for retreat. Anemone and Pappy also urge the others to run. Then a siege tower catches fire. Sajhan is still there, coated in burning tar and struggling to stay aloft. The tower is burning with her beside it.

Crossbow fire brings Sajhan down. She remains furious and tries to make her last burning weapon count, but the recovered text does not establish the result of that final throw. Her death is explicit: the enemy beheads her. The tower’s fire is a real blow against the Rahu, bought at a cost the company cannot recover by calling the raid a victory.

Brianna sends a flaming sphere against a catapult and starts another fire, then changes her action before it is irreparably burned. Anemone dies in Pappy’s arms, thinking of Olokun back in town painting Oya. Pappy relives an older loss, lays Anemone down and returns to the fight. He too falls dead. Ghilsen, in a transformed warrior shape, carries Brianna’s fallen body toward safety as her awareness fades.

One tower burns, but the bombardment has not been ended. Sajhan, Anemone and Pappy die in the failed sortie. Their later appearances, where other histories record them, cannot remove those deaths from this field. Nor does the surviving text provide a single explanation for every return.

Melian is missing

The next crisis begins at Melian’s house. Herb, Lilian and the raven lie dead nearby. Herb and Lilian have been struck by black-fletched arrows; the raven bears magical burns. The door is open. Melian is gone.

The investigation is posted on 5, Month of Rebirth, but its narrator places the scene on the preceding day, soon after the deaths were discovered. The search therefore belongs to 4, Month of Rebirth. That backdating concerns the investigation itself; it does not insert an extra day between discovering the bodies and examining the house.

Oya recognizes Herb, the man who made sandwiches, and breaks into tears. Serra remembers him as a father. Their loss is personal before it can become evidence. Inside are drafts of speeches about hope and courage, tea for two guests and a fallen chair. A little blood on the floor is Melian’s, left when she fell.

Magnus’s part in the abduction belongs to the wider established history. The searchers do not yet possess that whole account. Fulmin suspects him because of the magical burns; Eli warns that other people can use such magic and that these marks do not match his own experience of Magnus. Neither a suspicion nor Eli’s inability to identify the burns settles the attacker’s identity for them.

What the house can tell them

The tracks appear and disappear. Magical traces suggest the use of shadows. The disturbed room and Melian’s blood tell against an ordinary, willing departure. Oya comes to believe that the attackers meant to capture her; that conclusion is hers, built from what the group can see, rather than a message left by the captors explaining their orders.

A chemical trace offers another lead. Fulmin recognizes a gas associated with taking captives, and a bottle found in the search supports that identification. The bottle helps explain an abduction; it does not name the hand that used it. The sewers appear untouched. By the end Fulmin realizes that the defenses have been bypassed and that the town needs warning.

Oya asks whether anyone can speak with the dead. The scene does not provide a completed answer from the victims. Grief, physical traces and the attackers’ absence leave the investigators trying to act without the certainty later readers may wish they had.

Whom can the defenders trust?

The search opens another division when Lucido admits his Rahu allegiance. Fulmin draws his weapon and demands that he leave. Eli insists on judging what Lucido has done rather than condemning him by affiliation alone. Lucido renounces the Queen and the Rahu; the moment does not make him a witness to every part of Magnus’s involvement.

Oya hears the accusation widening toward her brother. She is alarmed to learn of Olokun’s former connection, but refuses to accept it as proof that he wants to harm Pristinia. She demands evidence. He practically raised her after their father died, she tells the others. The family history explains the force of her defense without giving her knowledge of everything he has done.

The same company must find Melian, warn a breached town and decide whether an old allegiance makes someone an enemy forever. Suspicion is understandable after the bridge. It is also capable of turning the searchers against one another while the captors remain absent.

Elenia and the unfinished siege

Elenia is remembered as the Savior of Pristinia for breaking the siege towers. That earlier success gives the town a reprieve, not an end to every Rahu position. The later quest opens with Fulmin recalling a previous battle alongside her and with the town still grieving Herb and Lilian and fearing for Melian. The stages must not be collapsed into one miraculous afternoon.

On 11, Month of Rebirth, the adventurers meet in a shelter protecting the tunnels the townsfolk built. This time they mean to seize the initiative. Olokun presents two aims: destroy the remaining engines or strike at commanders who may know where Melian is. Elenia suggests dividing the work; Olokun fears they are too few to divide safely. Arjahn argues that a siege camp may offer both a commander and machines.

They choose the engines. For Arjahn, grieving Sajhan, the decision is also a chance to finish the task she died attempting. Olokun and Eli move stealthily ahead while the more conspicuous companions draw attention. Rahu scouts spot them and ride away; Olokun catches one, but cannot prevent the others escaping. The camp is ready when they arrive.

The ground gives way

Elenia warns everyone to attack from a distance. Then the ground begins to shake. The earthquake envelops the catapults and breaks them into splinters. She backs into cover while maintaining the destruction. For Pristinia, which has spent the siege enduring stones thrown from beyond its walls, the machines’ sudden vulnerability changes the fight.

The defenders of the camp are still dangerous. Magical attacks strike Brianna; Arjahn struggles against incapacitating magic. Olokun, moving invisibly among the enemy, worries that their fire is falling on his exposed companions. He calls for Elenia to destroy the engines and take the less experienced adventurers out. Eli sees a last ballista tower standing at the rear.

That final machine is already weakened by the quake. Eli turns toward it, and it topples; Olokun sees him complete the work and moves back to support the others. Across the field, fissures swallow knights and archers. One archer falls into the lava below. Elenia’s magic has destroyed the machinery and made the ground itself lethal, but it has not made her companions invulnerable.

Olokun repeatedly calls for withdrawal. Elenia wants the nearby attackers dealt with first. The main objective is falling behind them in wreckage, and the battle is about to turn toward a familiar enemy instead.

The trial they cannot agree to hold

Magnus emerges from the shadows. Brianna recognizes someone she believed dead. Eli appeals to what Magnus once told him of his mother; Olokun beats him unconscious. Others are still falling. Alfred goes down with an arrow through his chest and regains his feet; Brianna and Arjahn are struck down. Elenia calls for healing, and Brianna wakes to the same field on which she has already watched companions die.

With Magnus helpless, the question becomes whether he will leave alive. Arjahn hates what he has done but wants him tried before Pristinia’s council. He remembers that Olokun too had belonged to the Rahu and argues himself toward mercy joined to judgment. Brianna acts first to preserve Magnus. Arjahn supports a trial, but asks why she had to let the prisoner wake.

Fulmin calls her aid treachery. Elenia reacts with horror. Brianna insists she is on Pristinia’s side and wants justice for those Magnus wronged. Olokun shouts for everyone to get away. Their dispute continues after the camp’s resistance is being finished, turning the escape into a confrontation among allies.

Brianna tries to carry Magnus off in animal form. Eli reaches the body, stabs it and burns its head to ash, saying he wants to prevent the soul from being brought back and corrupted. That is his stated purpose, not a newly proven law of resurrection. Elenia tells Brianna to leave the corpse and throws fire when she refuses. The narrator rules that Brianna must continue on foot rather than remain an eagle; her objection does not establish a successful flight.

No council trial occurs in this scene. The machines are destroyed, but the company cannot agree on how to secure an unconscious enemy, how to preserve a prisoner without returning him to combat, or who may make the final decision. The victory does not settle those questions for them.

Gathering the people they fought

When the fighting is over, Eli gathers weapons and armor for Pristinia to use or salvage. Arjahn goes back toward town, ashamed of his own weakness. Elenia asks whether they should collect the bodies and hold a ceremony. She says she is not used to fighting people.

Olokun helps her gather the dead. Together they stack the bodies, and Elenia sets the pyre alight. She prays to Cala, Nuru and any good power listening to accept those who followed orders or fought for what they believed. She is sorry that unity could not be reached peacefully.

The same cleric who opened the ground beneath the Rahu now tries to give their dead a resting place. Her prayer does not undo her choices in the argument over Magnus. It is what she does after them, with the destruction and the bodies still before her.

The town that remains

The later peace account carries the search for Melian to another kind of confrontation. Olokun insists that the delegation leave with her. Ephraith answers that the war is over and Melian has already been released. This remains the Queen’s report of an off-page handover; it does not supply Melian’s route home or the exact conditions of captivity. Read Melian’s captivity and the release report →

Pristinia survives through more than its greatest spell. Knights defend and evacuate; civilians shore up tunnels; friends carry the fallen; cooks and neighbors become the dead whom others must identify. The siege changes the place because it strikes at that ordinary life. Herb’s sandwiches, Lilian’s warnings and Melian’s unfinished speeches are part of what the company has been trying to save.

The Rahu war leaves different consequences in the people who remain. Magnus’s choices break old companionship. Brianna’s insistence on a trial repeatedly puts her against friends who fear another attack. Oya’s grief becomes a demand that accusation still require proof. Elenia’s destruction of the engines becomes civic memory, while the failed raids and shared defense remain part of the town’s survival. Continue with Pristinia’s wider history →
